title: Template, scene and treatment capability record
description: EXTENSION to the project's existing per-scene `selectionContract`, not a replacement. All 185 approved scenes already carry a selectionContract with requiredAssets, presentation, acceptedMedia, videoTreatment, usageModes, nativeDurationSeconds and retimeAllowed; the infographic and cinematic-scatter profiles carry richer capacity, data_mapping, visual_encoding, avoid_when and input_contract records. Reuse those field names where they exist. The fields this schema adds are the ones nothing currently records: timing.internalEvents (without which phrase alignment cannot be computed), slots.textSlots (whether a container can name an entity, date or source), adjustability.colour.method and exposedControlCount (auto-extractable from the .aep), narrationFit.maximumEvidenceObligation, styleProfile.motionLanguage as a checkable reading-load value, and capacity.portraitLegibilityLimit. It also proposes populating focalEntityCount, present on only 14 of 185 approved scenes today. Attribution fields are informational. User ruling 2026-09-16: record the source, do not require it on screen, and never filter a container on attribution capability.

kind.description: direct_media_treatment covers the non-template answers: a clean cut to archival footage, an uncut interview hold, a single image on screen. These must be records too, or the selector cannot compare a template against not using one.

pluginsRequired.description: A pack requiring a plugin the machine lacks is unusable regardless of fit.

count.description: extraction:auto from slot naming conventions such as 'Edit Image N', 'Media N', 'PLACEHOLDER N'.

cropBehaviour.description: fill_crop on a portrait asset is the mechanism behind the corpus's 'poor crops' rejection.

simultaneousVisible.description: How many slots are on screen at once, as opposed to in sequence. This is what decides whether a container can serve a group_comparative contract.

supportsDateLabels.description: Packs exposing 'Edit Date N' slots can carry chronology anchors natively.

supportsAttribution.description: Whether a source citation can be placed without overlapping the evidence. INFORMATIONAL ONLY. Per the 2026-09-16 citation ruling this must never disqualify a container: one with no text slot remains eligible for evidence passages.

dataSlots.description: Present on infographic and counter families.

capacity.description: Derived from slots, stated in contract terms so matching is direct.

canNameEntitiesOnScreen.description: False when textSlots.count is 0. A carousel with no text slot cannot serve a contract requiring mustBeNamedOnScreen.

canCarryProof.description: Corpus proof-role share by treatment: evidence_or_document 95%, infographic 52%, after_effects_scene 49%, counter 41%, spatial_or_cinematic_3d only 16%. Spatial scenes explain relationships; they rarely prove claims.

portraitLegibilityLimit.description: Entity count beyond which this container's portraits stop being identifiable, which is lower than its structural capacity. Surfaced by user feedback on passage 14: a six-card layout was accepted because 'it has nice size portraits given that were only talking about a handful of artists', while higher-capacity layouts were questioned. Nothing currently records this.

speedAdjustableRange.description: [min, max] multiplier that preserves readable motion. Speed adjustment is an approved adjustment; it is not permission to rescue a structurally wrong container.

internalEvents.description: The container's own beats. A contract event can only be aligned to a phrase if the container has an internal event that can be moved to that time. NOT PRESENT IN THE CURRENT CATALOG: timing control today is whole-scene retime (allowSpeedUp/allowSlowDown, outputDuration = nativeDuration / playbackRate), which fits a scene to a duration but cannot land a highlight on a word. Since phrase alignment is the project's stated highestPriorityGate, this is the most consequential missing field.

movable.description: Whether the beat can be retimed independently of the rest of the scene.

minimumReadableHoldSeconds.description: Shortest the container holds any element at native speed. If speeding the container to fit would push this below 1.5s, the adjustment is rejected.

narrationFit.description: The reverse direction. What narration can this container validly serve?

requiredClaimStructure.description: Plain language. 'One entity and a dated milestone per slot, in ascending order' is usable; 'good for timelines' is not.

maximumEvidenceObligation.description: The strictest obligation this container can honour. A container that crops, stylizes or overlays evidence cannot honour exact_source_required.

observedInReferenceUnits.description: Unit ids from the reference corpus showing this pattern working, e.g. 'r1:VU_136'. Every claim in this record should be traceable to evidence or marked as untested.

compatibility.description: The four-way distinction required by the brief. Do not collapse it to a boolean.

textureOverlays.description: Grain, scratches, dust, light leaks. Archival texture is an approved exception; a generic grunge overlay on a modern evidence document is not.

archivalException.description: True when this container is approved to present source material in its native appearance while its frame stays inside the dark cinematic system.

motionActivity.description: Checkable reading-load value. The global rule `readability` rejects scenes whose motion prevents reading, and user feedback on passage 17 distinguishes a scene that is the wrong kind ('isnt made for reading, more for viewing') from one that is the right kind but too active ('the animation on them is a little too active for expecting the viewer to read rules'). That is a threshold, not a boolean, and no scene record carries it.

adjustability.description: Only the four approved adjustments may be assumed: speed, text removal, text modification, and colour where the template exposes or safely supports it. Anything else needs separate verification and approval.

method.description: extraction:auto can distinguish exposed_color_controls by counting Color Control effects in the .aep. Only 53% of 180 scanned project files expose one at all, and in the Documentary and Archival category only 2 of 12 packs do.

structuralModification.description: Never assume this is available. A candidate depending on it must escalate to the user.

approval.description: Scenes from the two named style reference packs are unreviewed until the user approves them individually.
